security.title: Security Config
security.description: Manage the enterprise security path: identity ingress → tool visibility → policy/command enforcement.

sections.rolloutDescription: Unified controls for tool policy, command execution, identity ingress, and tool visibility. Audit-only records decisions without blocking; enforcement confirms, denies, or hides by policy. Changes take effect immediately after saving.
sections.permissionBaselineDescription: Default permission modes for sessions created from different entry points. Fixed by the system and not editable here.
sections.baselineDescription: System hard-deny rules and the readonly capability ceiling. View-only; administrators cannot relax them.

labels.hardDeny: Commands always denied by the system

hints.policyRollout: Controls whether general policy decisions (file I/O, workflow actions, high-risk tools, etc.) actually block requests. Audit only: evaluate and audit without blocking. Enforce: deny/confirm decisions stop execution.
hints.commandRollout: Controls shell/command tools only (bash, shell, cmd, PowerShell, SSH commands, etc.). Can be enabled separately from policy enforcement—for example, enforce commands first while leaving other tools in audit-only mode.
hints.ingressRollout: Controls whether Channel, HTTP, and workflow entry points require a valid identity. Off: skip ingress identity checks. Audit only: resolve identity but do not block. Enforce: reject entry when no valid identity is available.
hints.visibilityRollout: Controls which tools the AI can use under the current security policy. For example, in readonly mode, the agent cannot see hidden tools. Audit only: still show all tools, and only record which ones would be hidden. Enforce: actually hide those tools.
hints.filesystemRollout: Controls whether file tools run in audit-only or enforcement mode.
